continuity_scope: Christopher Paolini, Eragon, Alfred A. Knopf first trade edition (2003), ISBN 9780375826689. This pass covers only that original-English novel. Later Inheritance Cycle novels, Murtagh, companion works, films, games, author commentary, and variant editions are excluded.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Alfred A. Knopf first trade edition, 2003, ISBN 9780375826689.
Christopher Paolini official Book One metadata; used for series/Book One boundary only.

coverage_rule: Include the novel's named protagonist/dragon pair, named guide and travelling/rescue allies Brom, Murtagh, and Arya, and the named primary adversaries Durza and Galbatorix. Peoples, Rider order, languages, magic, institutions, places, artifacts, prophecies, and plot structures remain dimensions or terms, never character nodes.
omissions: All named characters outside the declared protagonist, travel/rescue-ally, and primary-adversary cohort, including Varden and dwarf/elf leadership and minor named figures.
All later-cycle material, Murtagh, companion works, adaptations, games, and author commentary.
Peoples, offices/orders, magic/languages, artifacts, places, the Empire, and prophecy as character nodes.
uncertainties: Publisher web material establishes edition/scope and first-novel orientation, but detailed character claims are located to the printed novel's chapter sequence; page numbers vary by printing.
The reading guide contains later-book prompts. They are excluded from every character and relationship claim here.
Violence, bereavement, captivity, coercion, and combat occur in the novel; descriptions remain non-graphic.
evidence_basis: The 2003 Knopf edition is the primary witness; citations use its chapter sequences alongside official Paolini and Penguin Random House metadata. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, or adaptation material is used.

supports: Knopf edition identity and original publication year.
Eragon's Rider inheritance, Saphira's telepathic partnership, Alagaesia, and conflict with the Empire.
